transcript:
Header:
Date/Time: 2026-12-20 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Omar Ruiz (Redwood SE), Lena Patel (Harbor CISO), Marco Silva (Harbor Cloud Architect), Jenna Park (Harbor Privacy Counsel)

Summary (auto): Customer is evaluating Redwood for a small EU-resident pilot; top concerns: ensuring customer prompts are not used to train models, KMS/BYOK support, region residency, audit log fidelity, and SOC2/ISO evidence. Redwood proposed a pilot on Dedicated in eu-west with BYOK and 30-day ephemeral retention as default; offered artifacts and follow-ups.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya, I'll lead today. Omar from our infra team is here for the tech bits.
[00:10] Lena Patel: Hi, Lena here, CISO at Harbor. We have a pretty tight compliance bar so we'll focus on data handling and assurances.
[00:18] Marco Silva: Marco, cloud arch. I'll vet the KMS flow and network topology.
[00:24] Jenna Park: Jenna, privacy counsel. We care about PHI/PII flows and the contractual prom— the word I want is "no training" assurances.
[00:33] Omar Ruiz: Great, hi all. Quick agenda: SOC2/ISO artifacts, RBAC/SSO, KMS/BYOK, prompt retention/no-train, audit logs, and deployment options.

[01:05] Maya Chen: First question — are you expecting Redwood to host the pilot in EU-only regions and do you require VPC peering or an on-prem option?
[01:14] Marco Silva: EU required. VPC peering ideal, but we can start with dedicated virtual network in your eu-west region. Low latency matters for our underwriting flows.
[01:23] Maya Chen: Okay. We can do Dedicated capacity in eu-west and support VPC peering or private link. We'll include that in the pilot SLA.

[02:05] Lena Patel: SOC2 — can you provide last audit evidence and scope? We need Type II covering production environment.
[02:12] Maya Chen: Yes — we'll share a redacted SOC 2 Type II report and ISO 27001 certificate. I'll attach them after the call.
[02:20] Lena Patel: Does that include your private deployment code path as well or only hosted?
[02:25] Omar Ruiz: The Type II covers our hosted control plane and the managed Dedicated offering; private on-prem deployments have a slightly different scope, we can annotate.

[03:02] Marco Silva: KMS — we need BYOK and prefer CMKs in our tenant. How do you do key wrapping, HSM, and rotation?
[03:12] Omar Ruiz: We support Bring-Your-Own-Key via supported cloud KMS providers. Keys stay in your control; we do envelope encryption — we never persist unencrypted secrets. Rotation follows your KMS policy; we store only wrapped keys. We can show Terraform examples.
[03:31] Marco Silva: Any HSM vendor lock-in? We use a mix of cloud KMS and HSM-backed keys.
[03:36] Omar Ruiz: No vendor lock-in on our side; as long as KMS speaks standard APIs. For HSM-backed keys we use the cloud provider wrapper. We'll send the integration guide.

[04:00] Jenna Park: Important: We need a contractual "no training" clause. Public statements are okay, but we need legal wording and an attestation on non-use of prompt data for model training.
[04:14] Maya Chen: Understood. We provide a no-training commitment for customers that opt-in (and it's on by default for Dedicated/Private). We'll send suggested contract language and a short attestation letter.
[04:26] Jenna Park: Is that retroactive to logs and caches? If we send PHI by mistake, will it be excluded from any training or retained?
[04:35] Omar Ruiz: We have configurable retention. Default for hosted customers is 30 days for logs but for Dedicated/Private we can set ephemeral retention (24 hours or zero) and disable retention for prompt bodies. Also, PHI handling can be restricted to not persist prompt text; only operational metadata is logged.
[04:58] Lena Patel: So you can guarantee prompt bodies won't be used to retrain models?
[05:05] Maya Chen: Yes — for Dedicated and Private customers we can guarantee no-training and configure the runtime to not surface prompts to any training pipelines. We'll provide an attestation.

[05:42] Marco Silva: Audit logs — we need per-request logs with request id, user, model variant, token counts, and whether content redaction happened. Retention up to 7 years for compliance. Can Redwood export to our SIEM?
[05:55] Omar Ruiz: We capture structured audit logs and can stream to your SIEM via secure syslog or S3 push with encryption. Retention windows are configurable; very long-term retention can be done with archival to your storage. We include request ids and token metrics; full prompt content is optional and can be redacted or excluded.

[06:35] Lena Patel: RBAC and SSO — enterprise SAML, SCIM? We need role separation: ops, dev, privacy, and read-only audit roles.
[06:44] Maya Chen: We support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning. RBAC is granular: role-based permissions for routes, model deployment, keys, and audit access. We can map to your AD groups.
[06:55] Marco Silva: How do you control who can export prompts?
[07:00] Omar Ruiz: Export controls are policy-driven. You can disable prompt export at the route or project level; only users with the 'export' permission can retrieve stored prompt bodies.

[07:30] Speaker 4: (inaudible) question about model variants and fallbacks — will fallback models ever send data externally?
[07:37] Omar Ruiz: Fallbacks remain within the same tenant; no external model hosting unless explicitly configured.

[08:10] Jenna Park: Data residency — if we require EU-only, are backups and logs guaranteed to stay in EU?
[08:18] Maya Chen: Yes, we can provision Dedicated clusters in EU regions and keep backups and logs in EU storage. We will note that cross-region failover is configurable and requires your approval.

[08:46] Lena Patel: Pen tests and vuln disclosures — do you provide a pen test report and vulnerability disclosure program?
[08:52] Omar Ruiz: We publish a summary of pen tests and have a VDP and a bug bounty program. We'll share the high-level results; some details are redacted for security.

[09:20] Maya Chen: Quick recap of commitments: we will send redacted SOC2/ISO artifacts, a no-training attestation, KMS integration docs, and set up a BYOK technical walkthrough. Any other must-haves?
[09:32] Marco Silva: Performance requirements for pilot — expected peak 200 RPS, p95 latency under 200ms. We'll include that in the pilot doc.
[09:40] Jenna Park: Also require legal attestation and ability to terminate data retention with 30 days notice.

[10:05] Maya Chen: Perfect. We'll follow up with artifacts and propose times for the technical deep-dive.
[10:12] Lena Patel: Thanks all.

[10:30] End of recorded transcript (remaining portion was scheduling logistics and calendar notes).
